decision: A track page with a spinning record, Play, and a now-playing bar, the pattern popularized by music-streaming apps, holds the analytics
why: A&R and marketing people think in songs, not dashboards; the song is the object, the numbers hang off it.
alternative: A metrics dashboard filtered by track.
value: The analysis opens where people already are: on the song.

decision: A full-width waveform from pre-computed JSON with a replay/skip heat strip underneath, and the playhead from the shared player
why: 'Hook 1:04–1:32 replayed by 38%' is only convincing when you can see where it sits in the song.
value: The cut decision is visible in one glance, with no audio bytes downloaded.

decision: Play uses the same <im-now-playing> element as Atlas, mounted in the Pulse layout, so playback continues across Pulse pages
why: One web component serves Next and SvelteKit; building a second player would double the code and the bugs.
value: Same behavior in two stacks, one implementation.

decision: Streams by market, the listener journey (impressions → plays → 30 s → saves → playlist adds) and playlist moves sit side by side
why: Growth in one market with a weak save rate is a different problem from strong saves and no playlists; the three views separate them.
value: Each stall in the journey points to a different fix.

decision: The AI suggests a 28 s vertical of the hook for Tokyo with its evidence, and approving only adds a draft to Distribution where the label approves again
why: Posting on an artist's behalf needs two keys: the marketer and the label.
value: Speed from the suggestion, safety from two approvals.
